explain.say: An African elephant's brain weighs around 5 kilograms, almost four times a human's, and the parts linked to memory are especially large. Only the biggest whales have heavier brains.

faq.q: How big is an elephant's brain?
faq.a: An African elephant's brain weighs around 5 kilograms, the largest of any land animal and nearly four times the weight of a human brain. Only big whales such as sperm whales have heavier brains.
asks: Which animal has the biggest brain?

faq.q: Why do elephant herds follow the oldest female?
faq.a: The matriarch has the most experience. She remembers distant water holes and safe routes from years before and knows which dangers are real, so families with older matriarchs survive hard times better.
Yes. Elephants know the contact calls of around a hundred other adults and can tell family from strangers by voice and smell, even after years apart.
Not literally, but their memories are long. They remember routes to water over decades, recognise many individuals and can remember people who treated them well or badly.
asks: Is it true elephants never forget?

faq.a: Elephants show strong interest in dead elephants, touching and smelling the body and bones with their trunks, and sometimes returning. Scientists debate whether this is grief, but it shows deep social bonds.

facts: In the 1993 drought in Tarangire, Tanzania, elephant families led by older matriarchs lost fewer calves (Foley and colleagues, 2008).
Female African elephants can recognise the contact calls of around 100 other adult elephants (McComb and colleagues, 2000).
